  - Asked: `widen` of a `ZZ` too large for `ZZ64` (row 502), which the natives meet when they bind `widen`: keep the low 64 bits, as walk does, or raise `IntegerOverflow` by the general sentence (row 349)? No default on record; the phase 3 exit judgement recommends the low 64 bits, before the natives bind `widen` (`reviews/phase3-exit/judgement.md`, section 5.2). PLAN item 31; review-queue item 20.
  - N3, C's 158: the 138 that need a new helper, sized at 132 helpers of about 0.7K lines in three rungs on the earlier count (`natives-shape.md`, section 3), and `IntLiteral`'s 20, which wait for N5.
  - N4, D1's 36, the I/O objects: a Java-backed writer type and `stdOut` first, since every program's `println` writes through `Writer`'s natives (F-32), then `File`'s 15 and `Reader`'s 10 (`natives-shape.md`, section 3).
  - N5, on the switch-over day, inside the names batch: the foreign-type table, the helpers' 55 raise strings, the `IntLiteral` helpers with the 24 `IntLiteral` bindings (4 of A, 20 of C; P-76; row 578), and the source files that name the prelude (`natives-shape.md`, section 3). N5 also drops the world test of fork 5's stand-in reading, once both paths read the one library (review-queue item 308).
  - D2's 42 wait: `NativeArray` with decision A (phase 5; P-84, P-85), and `Thread`, `Reflect` and `printTaskTrace`, off microGPT's path (F-32).

- The code generator over the one library (F-34): under the switch-over's setting it refuses 52 declarations of the library's twelve components, all of them declarations that the checker passes, measured once on climb batch 22's code (`reviews/phase3-exit/zero-audit.md`, "Part C. The debt carried into phase 4", item 4); each kind has a ledger row, among them a local function (row 304), varargs (row 624), "Not in the trait table" (row 733), a header `where` clause (row 701), and rows 818 to 823, `asif`, a postfix operator on a tuple operand, `Any` as a static argument in an `extends` clause, `try` with `forbid`, the kind env in a generic function's `typecase` and the `test` modifier (`perf-probes/codegen-distance/REPORT.md`, sections 2 to 6). The library must emit, not only check, before the compiled tests can run against it, so they are cleared before the prelude is deleted with its tests kept (P-37; `reviews/phase3-exit/judgement.md`, section 2.4): several rungs, which the planner sizes from the report's 14 kinds (the same, section 5.2, item 6). The judgement calls this phase 4's second zero, the code generator's over the same components as the checker's (section 6); it has not been measured over the fourteen. Code-generator work goes on beside P-33's order (P-33). Beside them, row 832, a generic dotted method whose single parameter has a tuple type, which the compile command's bound `Any` reaches and does not fix (F-296), is phase 4's by climb batch 22c's record (`coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-22c.md`, section 1, "What the batch leaves out").
- Row 701, the code generator's refusal of a declaration whose own header carries a `where` clause: five walls in the twelve, four of them lines the revival added, `SumReduction`'s `distribute`s (P-151), `BoundedRange.atMost` (P-156) and `AnyList`'s and `NatParam`'s restored `comprises ... where`, the fifth row 823's `test`; `fortress compile` on `FortressLibrary` stops at the first (the row; `reviews/phase3-exit/judgement.md`, item 9). A named code-generator rung before the names batch, by the judgement's default, which it gives the coordinator to take, and by the foundations judgement (`reviews/foundations/judgement.md`, section 5), as climb batch 22c's record placed it (`CLIMB-BATCH-22c.md`, section 1); review-queue item 182's "after the switch-over" is the earlier placement.
- Row 321: once the compiled path reads the one library, every object inherits the `getter toString` of its `trait Object`, so printing an object with no `asString`, which P-91 has print its bare Fortress type name, overflows the stack; a rung before the names batch (`reviews/phase3-exit/judgement.md`, sections 2.4 and 5.2, item 5; `reviews/foundations/judgement.md`, section 5; `CLIMB-BATCH-22c.md`, section 1). Asked with it, his word on the device that prints a tuple compiled: after the names batch the cast of `opr ||(a:String, b:Any)` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4488`) can raise `CastError` on a compiled `println((1, 2))`, since a tuple is no `Object` (P-42); a rendering native on `Any`, or the specification's `Tuple` trait (review-queue item 190)? Default, the judgement's: keep the cast now, file a row for the compiled tuple rendering, and decide the device in the names batch, one rung there (`reviews/phase3-exit/judgement.md`, item 14). No such row is filed yet.
- The components that microGPT imports outside the distance, checked report-only by climb batch 23's planner on both bases, the same 31 errors row for row: `System` 2, type errors of `NativeArray`'s immutable array (`Library/System.fss:28`, `:34`), `File` 4, `FileSupport` 24, `FortressAst` 1 (one export error over 203 generated objects), `FortressSyntax` 0 (`CLIMB-BATCH-23.md`, section 4, "The model's imports outside the distance"). By P-33, as his answer to review-queue item 283 has it: `System` by the switch-over, since the compiler's tests need it (F-293); each of the others before the first program that needs it, at the latest before walk runs the checker (P-12), so at the latest before microGPT, which imports them, compiles (phase 5). The library's other components (F-290) are cleared by the same rule. F-53's definition is unchanged (`reviews/batch-23-review.md`, finding 6).
- Asked: is `CompilerSystem`, the compiler's fourth library file, deleted at the switch-over with the prelude's three, and do the 28 programs that import it take the one library's `System`? P-37 names only the three files (F-293). Review-queue item 319, needed before the switch-over; default: nothing deletes `CompilerSystem` on P-37's strength until he answers, P-33's history reading his answer to item 283 as the file going with the prelude. Asked beside it, not in the item: 26 of the 28 import `args` by name and two the whole api (their import lines), and the one library's `args` reads `getProgramArgsPrim` (`Library/System.fss:28`, `:30`), a binding with no compiled analogue that `System` calls as it loads (D2; F-32), which `natives-shape.md` puts with `NativeArray` after the switch-over (section 3). Does that binding move by the switch-over, if the programs take `System`, or with `NativeArray` after it? No default on record.

N5 runs inside it (the natives above). Row 320, an api implemented by a component of another name, is part of its design (P-33), with re-approval row 41 and the nine dead sizes left (PLAN item 12; review-queue item 36). Rows 813 and 814 meet it: a name imported by name from one api read also on demand from another, and an `except` clause that leaves an infix operator imported ("Off the path, parked", "Phase 3's candidates at its end"; `reviews/batch-22-review.md`, finding 8). The `case` rule's compiler-world branch (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala:1397-1398`) and rung U's revision box (`Specification/basic/expressions/ranges.tex:102-109`) retire with the prelude (`reviews/batch-7R-conformance.md`, finding 3 and "The global questions").

**Consequential** means what the `coordinator` skill's `SKILL.md`, "The curator's role and decisions", gives: it reverses, bends or reads anew a decision of his; it touches microGPT's lines, speed or readability; it chooses among ways that the record does not settle, where the three principles split or are silent; or it cannot be undone.

### Question 1, consequential: the two top-level bindings declared over `String`

**Answered: option 1**, the default, by the coordinator at 09:4x UTC on 2026-10-31, from his scope: the two stay out of this batch, and his exclusion of the bindings over `String` stands until item 310 is asked again.

**The question.** His scope of 2026-10-31 names the small rest "`Long` 2, `BigNum` 2, top level 3, and the singletons that fit", and leaves out "the bindings over `String` (row 846; review-queue item 310, his default 'neither yet')". The last two are declared over `String`, and row 846 names them both: "The library's natives over strings take `FlatString`, but `printThreadInfo`, `printWithThread`, `printlnWithThread` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4628-4632`) and `getProperty` (`Library/System.fss:45`)".

**What stands.** Review-queue item 310 (PLAN item 62) keeps its default, neither, and is asked again before a binding over `String` moves (`40f08d22e`, "310 kept with its default, asked again before a binding over String moves"). **Taken: way 2b**, the hard-set probe's recommendation, by the curator's standing word of 08:2x UTC on 2026-10-31 (`coordinator/HELD.md`: "if he does not reply within half an hour of the probe's recommendation, the coordinator takes the probe's default into the batch"): asked at 09:54 UTC, no answer by 10:26. ### 3.2 `drandom` depends on the schedule (new)

**State.** `DeterministicRandom.deterministicRandomDouble` reads the worker's current task and advances that task's pedigree counter (`nativeHelpers/DeterministicRandom.java:52-56`, `runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java:108-111`). Each task has a depth, a unique `gamma` from its parent, and a `dotProduct` that every draw advances (`BaseTask.java:57-66`, `:83-94`, `:101-104`). The magic numbers are a fixed table (`useful/MagicNumbers.java:135`, `:394-396`), so on its own the scheme yields the same values in every run.

**Why it varies.**

- The current task is the worker's field `task` (`runtimeSystem/FortressTaskRunner.java:19`).
- Every generated `compute` sets it to its own task and never restores it (`compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:4753-4757`; the primordial task's, `:664-665`).
- `joinOrRun` saves and restores it only round a forked task's join (`BaseTask.java:165-173`). A task that was not forked runs inline through `this.compute()` (`:148-149`). It leaves the finished child as the current task for the rest of the parent's code.
- A new task takes the current task as its parent (`CodeGen.java:4686-4688`), so its `gamma` also comes from the finished child's counter.
- Whether a task is forked depends on the pool's queue (`BaseTask.java:113-116`, `:136-144`).

So which counters a draw advances depends on the schedule. This is not a data race: a task object is written only by the thread that runs as it. At one thread nothing inside the pool forks (`numThreads > 1` fails, `:114`), so, by reading, the values are fixed there. I did not run it at one thread: the brief allows runs at four threads only.

**The program**, `DrandomSched.fss`, compiled and run in the seeded worktree with `FORTRESS_CACHES` set to a private copy of its caches:

    component DrandomSched
    export Executable

    (* drandom at every node of a binary tree of tasks; the tuple forks the subtrees *)
    draws(d: ZZ32): RR64 =
      if d = 0 then drandom(1.0)
      else do
        (a, b) = (draws(d - 1), draws(d - 1))
        a + b + drandom(1.0)
      end end

    run(): () = do
      s: RR64 = draws(12)
      println("sum " || s)
    end
    end

    $ bin/fortress compile DrandomSched.fss                        # rc=0
    $ for i in 1 2 3; do FORTRESS_THREADS=4 bin/fortress run DrandomSched; done
    run1 threads=4: sum 4111.755423548555 rc=0
    run2 threads=4: sum 4111.368862987949 rc=0
    run3 threads=4: sum 4110.961144549375 rc=0

The machine: `nproc` 4, Intel Xeon Processor @ 2.10GHz (2100 MHz), load 0.69 at the start, OpenJDK 25 (`/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64`), `FORTRESS_THREADS=4`, no other Fortress JVM running.

**What it reaches.** Only the compiler's prelude binds it (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:1631-1632`). Walk's library has no `drandom`: its `random` is `Math.random()`, not reproducible by design. The model program draws no random numbers. The specification says nothing about random numbers: a `grep -i random` of `Specification/` finds nothing. The promise of determinism is the helper's name, and the team's pedigree comment (`BaseTask.java:57-61`). The team's test, `other_compiler_tests/deterministicRandomTest.fss` with `TestDrandom.test`, asserts only `PASS`.

**The record.** No ledger row knows it: `ledger.py find` on `drandom`, `deterministic*`, `nondetermin*`, `random` and `thread*` finds none. A draft row, for whoever writes the ledger, passes `ledger.py check --rows` except for its `?`. It is `CONTESTED`, because the specification is silent:

    | ? | the compiled `drandom` and `drandomZZ32` (`DeterministicRandom`) give values that depend on the schedule above one thread: a binary tree of tasks that draws at every node sums to a different value in each of three runs at `FORTRESS_THREADS=4` | CONTESTED | implementation gap (runtime) | silent | none | natives shared-state audit | A draw advances the current task's pedigree (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/DeterministicRandom.java:52-56`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java:108-111`); a compiled `compute` sets the current task and never restores it (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:4753-4757`), `joinOrRun` restores it only round a forked join (`BaseTask.java:146-177`), at 1f5c49b4f. `draws(12)` (`explorations/reviews/natives-shared-state-audit.md`, 3.2) printed 4111.755423548555, 4111.368862987949, 4110.961144549375. Contested: the specification is silent; the name and the pedigree comment promise it (`BaseTask.java:57-61`). |

**Transactions, by reading.** The same unrestored field resolves the current transaction (`BaseTask.java:180-201`, `:232-254`). A child copies its parent's transaction when it is made (`:86`), so the transaction follows the field, and I found no way for an inline child to change which transaction a write reaches. Pedigrees are what differ between a parent and its finished child. So `drandom` is the one place I found where the unrestored field shows.

### 3.3 The compiled task group's totals (new, by reading, not run)

`FortressTaskRunnerGroup.allRetries` and `totalElapsedTime` are plain fields of the one pool (`runtimeSystem/FortressTaskRunnerGroup.java:28-29`). `addRetries` and `addElapsedTime` add to them with an unguarded `+=` (`:36-42`). Every worker calls both at every `endTransaction` (`FortressTaskRunner.java:52-60`, from `BaseTask.java:200`). So two commits on two threads can lose an update.
## 6. For the report's reader

**Defects.**

- Row 855 (known): nothing new to add but section 3.1's three points.
- `drandom`'s dependence on the schedule (section 3.2): measured. No ledger row yet; the draft above.
- The compiled task group's unguarded totals (section 3.3): by reading, not reproduced. No ledger row; I drafted none, because nothing in the tree could reproduce it.

**Sentences of the specification made false.** None; nothing was changed.

**Decisions.**

- *Which race to show by the one program.* I chose `drandom`, the only new candidate that a program can show. The other candidates:
  - `NN32`'s path into the `ZZ64` scratch array, already in row 855's claim and fixed by rung K;
  - the task group's totals, which no program can check without an independent count.
- *Four threads only.* I ran the program only at four threads, as the brief allows, and argued its value at one thread by reading (section 3.2).
- *The draft row's status.* `CONTESTED`, not `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, because the specification is silent on random numbers (the row template, "status").
- *The ledger.* I wrote no ledger row: the brief asks for the note and its INDEX line only.
- *Scope.* The two directories, and what they call into one level down. I read the run times' tasks and transactions for their guards, not their correctness. No decision of the curator covers these choices.

**For FACTS.** One candidate, handed over:

- *The fact:* in `nativeHelpers/` and `interpreter/glue/`, the only state that a native's calls share and write with call-dependent values is the two `CHOOSE` scratch arrays. Every other static or shared field is a constant, set at load, or guarded.
- *What it means:* moving a binding onto an existing helper adds no parallel risk, except for the two `CHOOSE` helpers until rung K lands.
- *The number:* 2 fields, of the 688 compiled classes listed. Both are row 855.
- *What shows it:* no test. The `javap` command below, whose non-final fields are those of section 2.
- *Detail:* section 2 of this note.

**Commands** worked out here:

- The fields of the natives, from the built classes, in one JVM. A loop that starts one `javap` per class takes minutes.

      cd <base-build>/ProjectFortress/build/com/sun/fortress
      javap -p interpreter/glue/prim/*.class interpreter/glue/*.class nativeHelpers/*.class > all.txt
      awk '/(class|interface) [A-Za-z0-9_.$]+/{cls=$0} /^  [^(]*;$/ && !/ final / && !/static \{\}/{print cls " ::" $0}' all.txt

  Drop `!/ final /`, and keep the lines of object type, to see the `final` fields that hold a mutable object.
- A compiled run with a private caches folder in a seeded worktree: `cp -a default_repository/caches tmp/priv-caches`, then `FORTRESS_CACHES=$PWD/tmp/priv-caches` for both `bin/fortress compile P.fss` and `bin/fortress run P`. `bin/fortress_classpath` takes the jars from that folder (`explorations/coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh`, its header).

**Questions for the curator** (decisions not taken):

1. *Must `drandom` be deterministic?* The ways:
   - (a) restore the current task after an inline child too, in `joinOrRun` round `this.compute()` (`BaseTask.java:148-149`), as the forked branch does;
   - (b) record it as a property of the compiler's prelude, and do nothing;
   - (c) decide when the one library gains a deterministic generator, since `drandom` leaves with the prelude at the switch-over.

   Evidence: section 3.2. The default, if not answered: (b), with the draft row filed.
2. *The systematic check* of section 7: adopt it, a part of it, or neither.

## 7. For the curator: one slip or a pattern

**One slip in the natives' own state.** Of the 25 helper files, the 37 glue files and walk's native machinery, the two `CHOOSE` helpers alone keep state that their calls share and write with values that depend on the call (row 855). Every other static field is a constant, a value set while the program or an instantiation loads, a value rewritten only with the same value, or guarded by a lock or a `volatile` field used correctly. The team marked the one other scratch buffer as unsafe for parallel use, and it stays confined to one call. Walk's library binds 21 helper calls today, all pure functions of their arguments. No native on microGPT's path holds state that its calls share.

**The pattern is in the checking, not the code.** No test calls a native from parallel tasks and compares the results with a sequential answer. The gate's atomic runs exercise the compiled transactions and the first load of classes, and the suites run each test once at four threads. That is why row 855 waited for a probe. It is also why two neighbours are new today, both in the compiled run time's task state rather than in a helper's fields. The first is `drandom`, whose values depend on the schedule (three runs at four threads, three different sums). The second is the task group's unguarded retry totals, which only a diagnostic line shows.

**A systematic check (my proposal, not built).** Two parts:

1. *A static check in the gate.* List every field of the classes under `nativeHelpers/` and `interpreter/glue/` that is static and either not final or of an array or collection type, and every instance field of a glue class. Fail on any not in an allow-list taken from section 2 of this note. One `javap -p` over the built classes does it (section 6, "Commands"). It is about forty lines of script and the allow-list, a small worker's task, and it ran well inside 100 seconds here (not timed). It catches a new scratch buffer or cache in any helper that phase 4 writes or moves. It does not see state reached through calls, such as `drandom`'s; section 2's one level of calls would need reading again only when a helper starts calling into the run time.
2. *A parallel test for each helper with state.* For a helper that the check lets through with state, or that calls into run-time state, write a compiled test that calls its binding from a parallel loop at four threads and asserts each value against a sequential answer, as the `CHOOSE` probe's tests do (`plan-24/probes/choose.patch`). Today that is the two `CHOOSE` helpers, which rung K already covers, and `drandom` if question 1 asks for its determinism. A pure helper needs none: the static check is its proof. So the bindings that phase 4 still moves add no parallel tests unless their helpers keep state.

The cost: one small worker session for part 1, then one `javap` run in each gate, under 100 seconds here; for part 2, nothing beyond rung K's tests today, one test for `drandom` if question 1 asks for it, and one test for each stateful helper that appears later.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Checks explorations/coordinator/INDEX.md against the tree: which standalone
# notes are missing a line, which lines name a file that is gone, which lines
# fall outside the set the index is meant to cover, and which paths named in a
# line's prose no longer resolve. Read-only. Exit 1 if the first two are
# non-empty.
#
# The note set is every *.md under explorations/ except run/experiment trees
# (which document themselves in their own README) and evidence directories.
# Edit the two lists below when the shape of the tree changes.

set -uo pipefail

root=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
index="$root/explorations/coordinator/INDEX.md"
[ -f "$index" ] || { echo "no INDEX.md at $index" >&2; exit 2; }

# Run/experiment trees: a directory holding one run's sources and evidence.
run_roots='apl|astra|blinded-fable|compile-ladder|run-b|run-b2|run-c|run-c3|run-c4|fortify|ci|experiment'
# Generic evidence directory names, at any depth.
evidence_dirs='probes|checks|goldens|figures|evidence|measurements|raw|src|tools|gate|cold-cache|reference|archive|build|article|worker|notes|recovered-reports|_prior|__pycache__|existing-tests|failed|png|regen|tic-regen|tour|pairs|combos'

notes=$(cd "$root" && find explorations -name '*.md' \
  | grep -vE "(^|/)[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+-(probes|pairs)/" \
  | grep -vE "(^|/)($evidence_dirs)/" \
  | grep -vE "^explorations/($run_roots)/" \
  | grep -v '^explorations/coordinator/INDEX.md$' \
  | sort)

# Entry keys: the backticked path at the start of an index bullet.
keys=$(grep -oP '^- `\K[^`]+' "$index" | sort -u)
# Entry keys that are notes (drop the .js/.sh entries from the comparison set).
key_notes=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | grep '\.md$' | sort -u)

missing=$(comm -23 <(printf '%s\n' "$notes") <(printf '%s\n' "$key_notes"))
stale=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | while read -r p; do
  [ -n "$p" ] && [ ! -e "$root/$p" ] && echo "$p"
done)
outside=$(comm -13 <(printf '%s\n' "$notes") <(printf '%s\n' "$key_notes"))

POSITIONS.md:55
- P-58 **Every native binding is a `builtinPrimitive` call naming a static helper.** A native binding is a library body that is exactly `builtinPrimitive("…")`, the library's own form, and it keeps that form. Why: the language has no foreign-function interface, only a planned one, so the library's own practice decides the binding's form. Its string is to name a static Java method in `nativeHelpers/`, the compiled path's helpers, such as `"com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleIntArith.intLT"`, in place of a glue class of walk, which the compiled path cannot use (F-32). Walk is to load the named helper through a loader beside its glue classes. At the parse, before the checker, the compiled path is to rewrite each such body into a synthetic `import java` of the helper and a call, and to refuse a string that names no helper. The bindings move onto helpers step by step, and from the step that moves a binding, the compiled checker checks it against the helper's Java signature, not all at once at the switch-over. The other form, `import java` declarations written in the library itself, is not taken. F-32 counts the bindings that still name a glue class.

content.content:
## 2. What the specification says

- `Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex`, section "Integers", the method entry `opr CHOOSE(self, other: ZZ): ZZ` (`:606-616`): "The \OPR{CHOOSE} operator is defined only for natural number types; it computes the binomial coefficient \EXP{m \OPR{CHOOSE} n = m!/(n! (m-n)!)}. If \EXP{n<0} or \EXP{n>m}, the result is \EXP{0}." It also gives the property `FORALL (m,n: ZZ) (m CHOOSE n) + (m CHOOSE (n+1)) = ((m+1) CHOOSE (n+1))`. The result type was `NN` in the Working Draft of February 2011 and is `ZZ` here (`\revision{revival-integers}`, `:298-303`; Appendix I, "The integer trait").
- `Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex`, subsection "GCD, LCM, and CHOOSE Operators" (`:254-266`): "The operator \OPR{CHOOSE} computes binomial coefficients: \EXP{n \OPR{CHOOSE} k = \binom{n}{k} = { n! \over k!(n-k)! }}." Then: "On a fixed-size integer type, by the rule for integer results above, a result that the type cannot hold throws an \TYP{IntegerOverflow}". The rule above is in subsection "Multiplication, Division, Modulo, and Remainder Operators" (`:155`): "For integer results, overflow throws an \TYP{IntegerOverflow}."
- So on `ZZ32`, `CHOOSE` answers the exact coefficient where it fits in 32 bits and throws `IntegerOverflow` where it does not. P-73 applies this rule to `CHOOSE` by name: "The rule covers every operation whose result can leave its type, `^`, `CHOOSE` and `LCM` included". On the compiled path the rule holds as the specification's, "and the compiled path departs from it at `^` (rows 523 to 525) and at `CHOOSE` (row 521)".
- The specification says nothing about parallel calls of `CHOOSE`. The value it gives is the value at every call. Loops run in parallel by default (`Specification/basic/expressions/for.tex`, "For Loops"; the skill's "Parallelism and mutable state").

A side finding about the text, outside the helper: the property is false at `m = n = -1` under the entry's own zero rule. `(-1) CHOOSE (-1)` is 0 (n<0) and `(-1) CHOOSE 0` is 0 (n>m), but `0 CHOOSE 0` is 1. It holds at every other pair, including every `m ≥ 0`. Both paths give the zero rule's values: walk's glue and the helper both return 0 where `k < 0` or `k > n` (`Int.java:361`, `simpleIntArith.java:205`), so `(-1) CHOOSE (-1)` and `(-1) CHOOSE 0` are 0 on both. The Working Draft has the same text (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:567-574`). The words "defined only for natural number types" seem to mean the property for `m ≥ 0`. Section 9 lists this as a question; it does not bear on batch 24.

## 8. Decided by the record, or the curator's word?

The record decides the fix, and it needs no new word from the curator:

P-73 names `CHOOSE` under that rule, and on the compiled path holds it "as the specification's (P-25)", naming row 521 as the departure. F-132 is walk's half, as built. Row 521 names the fix: "throw `IntegerOverflow` when `k-2` is past the table's end". P-58 says the binding moves onto the helper. Climb batch 23's fork 12, at its default, kept `CHOOSE` on its glue class until that fix (`coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-23.md:43`, `:112`). The fork's other way named both helpers, `simpleIntArith` and `simpleLongArith`, so `XXXChooseTableCompiledRungE` is promoted only when the `ZZ64` half is fixed too (section 7.4).
